Day 1 · Sun 27 Sep

Colombo

Landing · 45 minutes to the hotel

You land mid-afternoon and go straight into the city. Taj Samudra sits on Galle Face, facing the open sea with the green in front of it — the one stretch of Colombo where the whole city comes out to walk at dusk.

Afternoon
Land at Colombo, 16:15Our driver meets us in the arrivals hall with a name board.
Evening
Check in at Taj Samudra, then the sea front
Night
DinnerWellawatte, ten minutes away, has the best South Indian food in the country.
Taj Samudra, Colombo · on Galle Face, facing the sea
Day 2 · Mon 28 Sep

Kandy

3½ hours inland, up into the hills
🎂 Birthday

The old royal capital, wrapped around a lake in green hills — and where the birthday lands. The Temple of the Tooth is the holiest Buddhist site in the country, and the evening ceremony — an hour of drummers, horns and people carrying lotus flowers — is the thing to be there for. Quite a way to spend a birthday evening.

Morning
Drive up, stopping at a spice gardenCinnamon, cardamom and pepper growing on the bush
Afternoon
Peradeniya Botanical GardensFlat shaded paths, huge old trees. No steps.
Evening
Temple of the Tooth for the evening ceremony, then birthday dinner
Cinnamon Citadel, Kandy · on the Mahaweli river. Pack before bed.
Day 3 · Tue 29 Sep

Nuwara Eliya

3 hours up · the hill station the British built

The strangest town in Sri Lanka, and the prettiest. The British built it as a hill station and it never quite stopped being one — a red-brick Tudor post office, colonial bungalows with rose gardens, a racecourse, log fires at night. They call it Little England. Six thousand feet up and cool all year.

Morning
Leave Kandy, up through the teaStopping at Ramboda Falls, and anywhere else worth stopping
Midday
Reach Nuwara Eliya, check in
Afternoon
The town on footThe post office, Victoria Park and Gregory Lake are all a short walk from the hotel
Evening
High tea at the Grand Hotel, then dinner
The Ramp · a seven-room hotel in the middle of town. Bring something warm — it drops to 10°C.
Day 4 · Wed 30 Sep

The mountain train

Rail to Demodara, then south to the coast

The old hill railway runs along the mountainside through tea gardens, tunnels and stone viaducts — often called one of the most beautiful train rides in the world. We stay on past Ella so the train carries us over the Nine Arch Bridge, then get off at Demodara and walk back to see it from below.

Early
Breakfast, then twenty minutes down to Nanu Oya station
09:00
The train leavesReserved seats, open windows. Pattipola at 1,891 m is the highest station in Sri Lanka.
Late morning
Across Nine Arch Bridge, off at DemodaraThe driver is waiting with the bags. Ten minutes back to see the bridge from underneath.
Afternoon
Lunch in Ella, then the long drive south to Galle
Two nights · Radisson Blu Resort Galle
Day 5 · Thu 1 Oct

Galle

No packing · the fort is fifteen minutes away

A day to enjoy the hotel, and then the fort. Galle Fort is four hundred years old and built out into the sea — cobbled lanes, a white lighthouse, old shuttered houses full of little shops, and wide stone walls you can walk right around. It works just as well in the rain.

Morning
The pool and the property. Nothing booked.
Afternoon
Into Galle FortThe lanes, the lighthouse, whichever café looks right
Sunset
On the ramparts, with the whole town out walking
Night
Back for dinner
Radisson Blu Resort Galle again · same room, nothing to pack
Day 6 · Fri 2 Oct

Koggala Lake

Thirty minutes along the coast to Ahangama

A short hop east, with a boat in the middle of it. Koggala Lake is a two-hour safari through mangroves to a temple island, with a cinnamon-peeling demonstration on the way — entirely seated, entirely shaded, no walking at all. The stilt fishermen are on the same road.

Morning

Midday

Check in at Ahangama

Sunset from the pool
Two nights · Villa H2O, Ahangama · private pool, by Secret Beach
Day 7 · Sat 3 Oct · Rest day

A day off

No packing, no driving, no schedule

The last full day, and nothing in it. Secret Beach is a boulder-protected cove a short walk away — the calmest water on this stretch of coast, and usually empty. Otherwise: the private pool, a long lunch, and the sunset.
